result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): B's diagnosis is a bit sharper: it points out the h1 serif / h2 sans / h3 serif swaps and adds body size and line-height to its CSS. But B's replacement CSS leaves out .phone-number from the font rule, so the phone number stays in Courier New, the issue B itself calls the biggest. B also wrongly says Courier has uneven digit widths, though it is a monospace font with equal-width digits. A's fix is complete, gives a real system font fallback list, and names clear jobs for each font. A's one slip is suggesting Lora for h1 and h3, which brings back some of the serif/sans switching. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers explain that too many overlapping families cause the messy look and recommend cutting down to Open Sans, with Lora as an optional heading serif. B is stronger on practical details: it gives a real system fallback stack, recommends 18px+ body text with more line spacing, and suggests tel: links. A says Courier New has 'uneven digit widths', which is wrong because Courier is monospaced. B has its own flaw: putting Lora on h1 and h3 but not h2 brings back the alternating heading styles it should be removing.
